# Spec §11 — decisions: Tips

Part of spec §11, *Decisions made — do not re-litigate*. The index of every decision is
[`README.md`](README.md).

These were made with no road map, from the owner's words of 2026-11-14: a tips dialog, a green
Tips button to the right of Export in the editor, an automatic ask on a usage-then-calendar
schedule, and a Settings section that turns the ask and the button off. The owner called the
button an experiment that may be removed.

- **TIP-1 — A tip is voluntary, nothing in Frame Job is gated on one, and the app holds no payment
  code: the dialog says who a tip funds and opens one web page.** The statement is plain: Frame
  Job is made by one developer, it is free to use and its source is open, a tip helps pay for the
  time to keep working on it, and nothing is locked without one. "Leave a Tip" opens
  `https://boppallewyn.com/frame-job/tips/` in the person's browser, and that address is ONE
  constant (`TipsLink.url`, `Tips.swift`), so moving the page is a one-line change. The page is
  the owner's to make. Frame Job never learns whether anyone tipped, so there is no "thank you"
  state and nothing to restore. Risk accepted: until the page exists the button opens a missing
  page.
- **TIP-2 — The dialog is its own small window titled "Tips", not a sheet and not an app-modal
  alert, and it has three doors: the editor's Tips button, Settings' Tips button and the automatic
  ask.** A sheet needs a host window and two of the doors have no document (Settings, and Settings
  opened from the Welcome window); an app-modal alert would stop every window and would sit in
  front of an MCP client's calls. A window that is modal to nothing cannot make anything wait. It
  is the Settings window's mould (`TipsWindowController`): one instance, not released when closed,
  no frame autosave name (so it writes no `NSWindow Frame` key), built from the sheets' own pieces
  (`makeSheetView`, `makeButtonRow`) so it reads as one of them, Escape on "Not Now" and Return on
  "Leave a Tip". It is left out of the Window menu: a two-button dialog is not a place to come
  back to, and both buttons reopen it. There is no menu item for it, and no MCP mirror, because
  showing it is not an edit (spec §7.9).
- **TIP-3 — The automatic ask is due by usage first and the calendar after: never while the
  toggle is off; first once at least 5 exports are counted AND at least 30 × 24 hours have passed
  since the first counted export; after an ask, only in a December, and a December is skipped
  whole when its 1 December 00:00 is less than six calendar months after the last ask.** The rule
  is one pure function, `TipsSchedule.isDue(_:now:calendar:)`, over the stored state, the moment
  and a calendar. "30 days of use" counts from the first counted export and not from the first
  launch: a launch is also what `framejob-mcp` and every proof make, and a date stamped at launch
  would count use by agents alone. It is elapsed time, not thirty separate days of use, which
  would make an occasional user wait a year. "December" is month 12 of the GREGORIAN calendar in
  the Mac's current time zone (`TipsSchedule.localCalendar()`, built at each evaluation), whatever
  calendar the person's Mac shows, so the same instant can be December in Auckland and November
  in Los Angeles. A December is judged whole so that an ask on 30 June cannot bring the next one
  on 30 December: a last ask after 1 June 00:00 skips that year's December, and one at or before
  it does not. A clock set back before the last ask or the first export makes nothing due. Risk
  accepted: the rule is evaluated only when a counted export completes (TIP-4), so a person who
  exports nothing in December is not asked that year.
- **TIP-4 — Only an export a person confirmed in the export card counts, and only its completion
  evaluates the ask; the agent's `export` never does either.** The card's two commits both sit
  behind its save panel (`ExportSheetCommit.swift`), which no tool and no dev switch answers:
  Export… (`EditorViewController.beginExport`) and Add to Queue (`enqueueExport`). The first hands
  the progress sheet an `onSuccess` it calls once, on a success only; the second follows its job
  by the id `enqueue` answered (`TipsQueueFollower`, `AgentExports`' pattern), so
  `ExportQueueController` is not changed and its jobs carry no origin. The agent's `export`
  enqueues on the same queue and is never followed, and the Assistant tab's `export` is that same
  door. So an instance driven only by an MCP client, the assistant or a proof counts nothing,
  writes no key and is never shown the dialog, which is what keeps `mcp.py`'s `DEFAULTS MOVED`
  guard quiet. A counted export is counted when it succeeds. The ask is evaluated, and recorded,
  at the moment it is shown: for Export…, when the result sheet ends (Close or Show in Finder),
  one main-queue turn later; for a queued job, when it completes. The automatic ask is ordered
  front WITHOUT becoming key, so a Return typed into the editor can never press "Leave a Tip";
  the two buttons' doors make it key. Risks accepted: after Show in Finder the dialog appears
  behind Finder and is found on return; a window closed with its result sheet still attached
  never ends that sheet, so that export is counted and the ask waits for the next one.
- **TIP-5 — The state is four keys of the bundle's defaults domain, written only at a person's
  doors.** `FrameJobTips` (Bool, absent means on) is the toggle, written by Settings' checkbox.
  `FrameJobTipsExports` (Int) and `FrameJobTipsFirstExport` (a date, stamped once) are written
  when a counted export succeeds, and counting goes on while the toggle is off, so turning it back
  on behaves sensibly. `FrameJobTipsLastAsked` (a date) is written when the automatic ask is shown
  and when "Leave a Tip" is pressed from any door: someone who has just visited the page is not
  asked again that December. Opening the dialog by hand and choosing "Not Now", or closing it,
  writes nothing. Dates are stored as dates, so `defaults write … -date` sets one. No project
  format changes. Risk accepted: the state is per Mac and per build identity, so a Debug build
  and a reinstall on another Mac each start again.
- **TIP-6 — The editor's Tips button is an `AccentButton` filled with `DS.tips` (`#2E7D32`), right
  of Export…, and Settings ▸ Tips holds the toggle that removes it.** The owner asked for green.
  The fill is a fixed leaf green, the same in both appearances as the recorder's coral Record
  button is, with the white `DS.onAccent` label at 5.1:1. It is deliberately not `DS.action` and
  not `DS.forest`: CI-4 keeps mint for the action ink and nothing else, and forest (`#1F8564`) is
  within 10/255 of the action ink's light value (`#1E8F6E`), so a forest button would read as an
  action in the light appearance. `DS.tips` sits about 40° of hue from both action values, so
  CI-4 stands unamended. How it looks is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`. The button is 12 pt
  after Export… with no rule between them, has no symbol, and is `TipsToolbarButton`, a view that
  hides itself while the toggle is off and follows `TipsSettings.didChangeNotification`, so the
  frozen editor file holds nothing for it: removing the experiment is deleting that file and one
  line of `buildToolbar`. Settings' fifth and last pane, "Tips", is a bare heading, one visible
  sentence (under SH-5's and `settings_layout_probe` L5's 200 characters, so it needs no ⓘ), the
  checkbox "Show the Tips button and the yearly reminder" (on by default) and a "Tips" button.
  Unticking stops the automatic ask and removes the button from every open editor at once; the
  pane's own button is never hidden or disabled and shows the dialog whatever the toggle says. It
  is a person's setting: no tool reads or writes it (R6-12, MC-7).
- **TIP-7 — The feature has no `-RCDev` switch and no dev tool, and its proof is a probe.**
  `tools/proof/tips_proof.py` builds `tips_probe.swift` over `app/Sources` and hands the schedule
  its clock, calendar and a scratch defaults suite; the two export doors are run for real, on a
  document made in process, with the ask, the window and the queue injected (`TipsDoors`), and the
  window's two order calls are closures so "front, not key" can be read where no probe window is
  ever key. A person pins state with `defaults write` (`docs/manual-checks.md`). So Debug, Release
  and Distribution run the same code. The offscreen harness pins `FrameJobTips` OFF: older chrome
  proofs read the toolbar at fixed points (`sharp_chrome.py`'s `EXPORT_RIGHT`,
  `phase7_chrome.py`'s accent patch) and a button right of Export… would move them; `screens.py`
  pins it ON, the first-run state the catalog shows, and lists the other three keys in
  `NOT_SHOWN`. The proof's live instances launch with `-FrameJobTips YES` or `NO`, so the owner's
  own toggle never decides a row. It holds twelve mutants, two past the usual ten, because the
  feature adds twelve separable decisions (two thresholds, the toggle, the month, the skip, the
  recorded ask, which queue states count, the agent's door, the button's and the pane's halves of
  the toggle, the success wiring and the order call) and dropping one would leave a decision no
  row is seen failing for.

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Tips (spec §11 TIP-1…TIP-7): what the dialog links to, when Frame Job asks
4	/// by itself, and what it remembers. Foundation only, so a probe can run the
5	/// rule against a clock of its own and the AppKit-free export queue can be
6	/// followed from here. The dialog is `TipsWindowController.swift`, the
7	/// editor's button `TipsToolbarButton.swift`, Settings' pane
8	/// `TipsSettingsPane.swift`.
9	
10	/// The one address "Leave a Tip" opens (TIP-1). The page is the owner's.
11	enum TipsLink {
12	    static let url = "https://boppallewyn.com/frame-job/tips/"
13	}
14	
15	/// What the schedule is decided from: the stored state, read at one moment.
16	struct TipsState: Equatable {
17	    /// When the first counted export succeeded; nil before one has.
18	    var firstExport: Date?
19	    /// How many exports a person confirmed in the export card have succeeded.
20	    var exports = 0
21	    /// When the automatic ask was last shown, or "Leave a Tip" last pressed.
22	    var lastAsked: Date?
23	    /// Settings ▸ Tips' toggle.
24	    var enabled = true
25	}
26	
27	/// When the automatic ask is due (TIP-3). Pure: the state, a moment and a
28	/// calendar in, a Bool out.
29	enum TipsSchedule {
30	    static let firstAskDays = 30
31	    static let firstAskExports = 5
32	    static let skipMonths = 6
33	
34	    /// The Gregorian calendar in the Mac's time zone as it is now, whatever
35	    /// calendar the person's Mac shows: "December" is its month 12.
36	    static func localCalendar() -> Calendar {
37	        var calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)
38	        calendar.timeZone = TimeZone.current
39	        return calendar
40	    }
41	
42	    /// Off is never due. The first ask waits for `firstAskExports` exports
43	    /// and `firstAskDays` days since the first of them. After an ask, only a
44	    /// December is due, and not one whose 1 December 00:00 is less than
45	    /// `skipMonths` calendar months after the last ask.
46	    static func isDue(_ state: TipsState, now: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> Bool {
47	        guard state.enabled else { return false }
48	        guard let first = state.firstExport else { return false }
49	        guard state.exports >= firstAskExports else { return false }
50	        guard now.timeIntervalSince(first) >= Double(firstAskDays) * 86_400 else { return false }
51	        guard let last = state.lastAsked else { return true }
52	        guard calendar.component(.month, from: now) == 12 else { return false }
53	        let year = calendar.component(.year, from: now)
54	        guard
55	            let december = calendar.date(from: DateComponents(year: year, month: 12, day: 1)),
56	            let earliest = calendar.date(byAdding: .month, value: skipMonths, to: last)
57	        else { return false }
58	        return earliest <= december
59	    }
60	}
61	
62	/// Settings ▸ Tips' toggle (TIP-5, TIP-6): on shows the editor's Tips button
63	/// and lets the automatic ask happen.
64	enum TipsSettings {
65	    /// Bool; absent = true.
66	    static let enabledKey = "FrameJobTips"
67	
68	    /// Posted after the toggle is written, so every editor's Tips button
69	    /// follows it at once.
70	    static let didChangeNotification = Notification.Name("FrameJobTipsSettingsDidChange")
71	
72	    static func isEnabled(in defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) -> Bool {
73	        defaults.object(forKey: enabledKey) == nil ? true : defaults.bool(forKey: enabledKey)
74	    }
75	
76	    /// Writes the toggle and posts `didChangeNotification`.
77	    static func setEnabled(_ enabled: Bool, in defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) {
78	        defaults.set(enabled, forKey: enabledKey)
79	        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: didChangeNotification, object: nil)
80	    }
81	}
82	
83	/// The stored state and its three writers (TIP-5). Every writer is reached
84	/// only from a person's door: an export confirmed in the export card, or the
85	/// dialog's "Leave a Tip". Main thread.
86	final class TipsAsk {
87	    /// Int; absent = 0.
88	    static let exportsKey = "FrameJobTipsExports"
89	    /// A date, stamped by the first counted export and never again.
90	    static let firstExportKey = "FrameJobTipsFirstExport"
91	    /// A date: the last automatic ask, or the last press of "Leave a Tip".
92	    static let lastAskedKey = "FrameJobTipsLastAsked"
93	
94	    /// The app's own, over the bundle's defaults and the real clock.
95	    static let shared = TipsAsk()
96	
97	    private let defaults: UserDefaults
98	    private let now: () -> Date
99	    private let calendar: () -> Calendar
100	
101	    init(
102	        defaults: UserDefaults = .standard, now: @escaping () -> Date = { Date() },
103	        calendar: @escaping () -> Calendar = { TipsSchedule.localCalendar() }
104	    ) {
105	        self.defaults = defaults
106	        self.now = now
107	        self.calendar = calendar
108	    }
109	
110	    var state: TipsState {
111	        TipsState(
112	            firstExport: defaults.object(forKey: Self.firstExportKey) as? Date,
113	            exports: defaults.integer(forKey: Self.exportsKey),
114	            lastAsked: defaults.object(forKey: Self.lastAskedKey) as? Date,
115	            enabled: TipsSettings.isEnabled(in: defaults))
116	    }
117	
118	    /// One more export a person confirmed has succeeded. Counts whatever the
119	    /// toggle says.
120	    func countExport() {
121	        let state = self.state
122	        defaults.set(state.exports + 1, forKey: Self.exportsKey)
123	        if state.firstExport == nil { defaults.set(now(), forKey: Self.firstExportKey) }
124	    }
125	
126	    /// True when the automatic ask is due now, and then it is recorded as
127	    /// asked, so the caller shows the dialog and a second call answers false.
128	    func takeAsk() -> Bool {
129	        let moment = now()
130	        guard TipsSchedule.isDue(state, now: moment, calendar: calendar()) else { return false }
131	        defaults.set(moment, forKey: Self.lastAskedKey)
132	        return true
133	    }
134	
135	    /// "Leave a Tip" was pressed, from any door: that is an ask too.
136	    func noteTipPageOpened() {
137	        defaults.set(now(), forKey: Self.lastAskedKey)
138	    }
139	}

141	/// Which export queue jobs a person started (Add to Queue), followed by id as
142	/// `AgentExports` follows the agent's, so the queue's jobs carry no origin
143	/// (TIP-4). `settle()` runs on every change of the queue.
144	final class TipsQueueFollower {
145	    private let state: (UInt64) -> ExportQueueController.State?
146	    private let completed: () -> Void
147	    private(set) var followed: Set<UInt64> = []
148	
149	    init(state: @escaping (UInt64) -> ExportQueueController.State?, completed: @escaping () -> Void)
150	    {
151	        self.state = state
152	        self.completed = completed
153	    }
154	
155	    func follow(_ id: UInt64) {
156	        followed.insert(id)
157	        settle()
158	    }
159	
160	    /// A followed job that completed calls `completed` once and is dropped;
161	    /// one cancelled, failed or gone from the list is dropped; one waiting or
162	    /// running stays.
163	    func settle() {
164	        for id in followed.sorted() {
165	            switch state(id) {
166	            case .completed:
167	                followed.remove(id)
168	                completed()
169	            case .cancelled, .failed, nil:
170	                followed.remove(id)
171	            case .waiting, .running:
172	                break
173	            }
174	        }
175	    }
176	}

140	/// the only caller; the agent's `export` never comes here. The ask, the
141	/// dialog and the queue are parameters so a probe runs both doors on its own.
142	/// Main thread.
143	final class TipsDoors {
144	    static let shared = TipsDoors()
145	
146	    private let ask: TipsAsk
147	    private let dialog: () -> TipsWindowController
148	    private let queue: ExportQueueController
149	    private var follower: TipsQueueFollower?
150	    private var queueObserver: NSObjectProtocol?
151	    /// The result sheets still up after a counted success, each waiting for
152	    /// its window's sheet to end.
153	    private var sheetEnds: [TipsSheetEnd] = []
154	
155	    init(
156	        ask: TipsAsk = .shared,
157	        dialog: @escaping () -> TipsWindowController = { TipsWindowController.shared },
158	        queue: ExportQueueController = .shared
159	    ) {
160	        self.ask = ask
161	        self.dialog = dialog
162	        self.queue = queue
163	    }
164	
165	    deinit {
166	        if let queueObserver { NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(queueObserver) }
167	    }
168	
169	    /// An Export… the person confirmed has succeeded: counted now. The ask
170	    /// waits until `window`'s sheet — the export's own result panel — ends,
171	    /// and one main-queue turn more so the sheet has left; with no sheet
172	    /// attached it is asked at once.
173	    func exportSucceeded(sheetOn window: NSWindow?) {
174	        ask.countExport()
175	        guard let window, window.attachedSheet != nil else {
176	            askIfDue()
177	            return
178	        }
179	        sheetEnds.append(
180	            TipsSheetEnd(window: window) { [weak self] watch in
181	                guard let self else { return }
182	                self.sheetEnds.removeAll { $0 === watch }
183	                self.askIfDue()
184	            })
185	    }
186	
187	    /// An Add to Queue job the person confirmed: followed to its end by id.
188	    /// A completion counts and asks; a cancel or a failure does neither.
189	    func follow(queueJob id: UInt64) {
190	        if follower == nil {
191	            follower = TipsQueueFollower(
192	                state: { [queue] in queue.job($0)?.state },
193	                completed: { [weak self] in
194	                    self?.ask.countExport()
195	                    self?.askIfDue()
196	                })
197	            queueObserver = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
198	                forName: ExportQueueController.didChangeNotification, object: queue, queue: nil
199	            ) { [weak self] _ in self?.follower?.settle() }
200	        }
201	        follower?.follow(id)
202	    }
203	
204	    /// Shows the dialog when the schedule says so, recording the ask at the
205	    /// moment it is shown.
206	    private func askIfDue() {
207	        guard ask.takeAsk() else { return }
208	        dialog().showAutomatic()
209	    }
210	}
211	
212	/// One wait for a window's sheet to end, then one main-queue turn.
213	private final class TipsSheetEnd: NSObject {
214	    private let then: (TipsSheetEnd) -> Void
215	
216	    init(window: NSWindow, then: @escaping (TipsSheetEnd) -> Void) {
217	        self.then = then
218	        super.init()
219	        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
220	            self, selector: #selector(ended(_:)), name: NSWindow.didEndSheetNotification,
221	            object: window)
222	    }
223	
224	    @objc private func ended(_ note: Notification) {
225	        NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(self)
226	        DispatchQueue.main.async { self.then(self) }
227	    }
228	}

234	/// the editor's Tips button resolves it through the responder chain.
235	extension AppDelegate {

238	    }

2	
3	/// Tips (spec §11 TIP-1…TIP-7): what the dialog links to, when Frame Job asks
4	/// by itself, and what it remembers. Foundation only, so a probe can run the
5	/// rule against a clock of its own and the AppKit-free export queue can be
6	/// followed from here. The dialog is `TipsWindowController.swift`, the
7	/// editor's button `TipsToolbarButton.swift`, Settings' pane
8	/// `TipsSettingsPane.swift`.
9	
10	/// The one address "Leave a Tip" opens (TIP-1). The page is the owner's.
11	enum TipsLink {
12	    static let url = "https://boppallewyn.com/frame-job/tips/"
13	}
14	
15	/// What the schedule is decided from: the stored state, read at one moment.
16	struct TipsState: Equatable {
17	    /// When the first counted export succeeded; nil before one has.
18	    var firstExport: Date?
19	    /// How many exports a person confirmed in the export card have succeeded.
20	    var exports = 0
21	    /// When the automatic ask was last shown, or "Leave a Tip" last pressed.
22	    var lastAsked: Date?
23	    /// Settings ▸ Tips' toggle.
24	    var enabled = true
25	}
26	
27	/// When the automatic ask is due (TIP-3). Pure: the state, a moment and a
28	/// calendar in, a Bool out.
29	enum TipsSchedule {
30	    static let firstAskDays = 30
31	    static let firstAskExports = 5
32	    static let skipMonths = 6
33	
34	    /// The Gregorian calendar in the Mac's time zone as it is now, whatever
35	    /// calendar the person's Mac shows: "December" is its month 12.
36	    static func localCalendar() -> Calendar {
37	        var calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)
38	        calendar.timeZone = TimeZone.current
39	        return calendar
40	    }
41	
42	    /// Off is never due. The first ask waits for `firstAskExports` exports
43	    /// and `firstAskDays` days since the first of them. After an ask, only a
44	    /// December is due, and not one whose 1 December 00:00 is less than
45	    /// `skipMonths` calendar months after the last ask.
46	    static func isDue(_ state: TipsState, now: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> Bool {
47	        guard state.enabled else { return false }
48	        guard let first = state.firstExport else { return false }
49	        guard state.exports >= firstAskExports else { return false }
50	        guard now.timeIntervalSince(first) >= Double(firstAskDays) * 86_400 else { return false }
51	        guard let last = state.lastAsked else { return true }
52	        guard calendar.component(.month, from: now) == 12 else { return false }
53	        let year = calendar.component(.year, from: now)
54	        guard
55	            let december = calendar.date(from: DateComponents(year: year, month: 12, day: 1)),
56	            let earliest = calendar.date(byAdding: .month, value: skipMonths, to: last)
57	        else { return false }
58	        return earliest <= december
59	    }
60	}
61	
62	/// Settings ▸ Tips' toggle (TIP-5, TIP-6): on shows the editor's Tips button
63	/// and lets the automatic ask happen.
64	enum TipsSettings {
65	    /// Bool; absent = true.
66	    static let enabledKey = "FrameJobTips"
67	
68	    /// Posted after the toggle is written, so every editor's Tips button
69	    /// follows it at once.
70	    static let didChangeNotification = Notification.Name("FrameJobTipsSettingsDidChange")
71	
72	    static func isEnabled(in defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) -> Bool {
73	        defaults.object(forKey: enabledKey) == nil ? true : defaults.bool(forKey: enabledKey)
74	    }
75	
76	    /// Writes the toggle and posts `didChangeNotification`.
77	    static func setEnabled(_ enabled: Bool, in defaults: UserDefaults = .standard) {
78	        defaults.set(enabled, forKey: enabledKey)
79	        NotificationCenter.default.post(name: didChangeNotification, object: nil)
80	    }
81	}
82	
83	/// The stored state and its three writers (TIP-5). Every writer is reached
84	/// only from a person's door: an export confirmed in the export card, or the
85	/// dialog's "Leave a Tip". Main thread.
86	final class TipsAsk {
87	    /// Int; absent = 0.
88	    static let exportsKey = "FrameJobTipsExports"
89	    /// A date, stamped by the first counted export and never again.
90	    static let firstExportKey = "FrameJobTipsFirstExport"
91	    /// A date: the last automatic ask, or the last press of "Leave a Tip".
92	    static let lastAskedKey = "FrameJobTipsLastAsked"
93	
94	    /// The app's own, over the bundle's defaults and the real clock.
95	    static let shared = TipsAsk()
96	
97	    private let defaults: UserDefaults
98	    private let now: () -> Date
99	    private let calendar: () -> Calendar
100	
101	    init(
102	        defaults: UserDefaults = .standard, now: @escaping () -> Date = { Date() },
103	        calendar: @escaping () -> Calendar = { TipsSchedule.localCalendar() }
104	    ) {
105	        self.defaults = defaults
106	        self.now = now
107	        self.calendar = calendar
108	    }
109	
110	    var state: TipsState {
111	        TipsState(
112	            firstExport: defaults.object(forKey: Self.firstExportKey) as? Date,
113	            exports: defaults.integer(forKey: Self.exportsKey),
114	            lastAsked: defaults.object(forKey: Self.lastAskedKey) as? Date,
115	            enabled: TipsSettings.isEnabled(in: defaults))
116	    }
117	
118	    /// One more export a person confirmed has succeeded. Counts whatever the
119	    /// toggle says.
120	    func countExport() {
121	        let state = self.state
122	        defaults.set(state.exports + 1, forKey: Self.exportsKey)
123	        if state.firstExport == nil { defaults.set(now(), forKey: Self.firstExportKey) }
124	    }
125	
126	    /// True when the automatic ask is due now, and then it is recorded as
127	    /// asked, so the caller shows the dialog and a second call answers false.
128	    func takeAsk() -> Bool {
129	        let moment = now()
130	        guard TipsSchedule.isDue(state, now: moment, calendar: calendar()) else { return false }
131	        defaults.set(moment, forKey: Self.lastAskedKey)
132	        return true
133	    }
134	
135	    /// "Leave a Tip" was pressed, from any door: that is an ask too.
136	    func noteTipPageOpened() {
137	        defaults.set(now(), forKey: Self.lastAskedKey)
138	    }
139	}

141	/// Which export queue jobs a person started (Add to Queue), followed by id as
142	/// `AgentExports` follows the agent's, so the queue's jobs carry no origin
143	/// (TIP-4). `settle()` runs on every change of the queue.
144	final class TipsQueueFollower {
145	    private let state: (UInt64) -> ExportQueueController.State?
146	    private let completed: () -> Void
147	    private(set) var followed: Set<UInt64> = []
148	
149	    init(state: @escaping (UInt64) -> ExportQueueController.State?, completed: @escaping () -> Void)
150	    {
151	        self.state = state
152	        self.completed = completed
153	    }
154	
155	    func follow(_ id: UInt64) {
156	        followed.insert(id)
157	        settle()
158	    }
159	
160	    /// A followed job that completed calls `completed` once and is dropped;
161	    /// one cancelled, failed or gone from the list is dropped; one waiting or
162	    /// running stays.
163	    func settle() {
164	        for id in followed.sorted() {
165	            switch state(id) {
166	            case .completed:
167	                followed.remove(id)
168	                completed()
169	            case .cancelled, .failed, nil:
170	                followed.remove(id)
171	            case .waiting, .running:
172	                break
173	            }
174	        }
175	    }
176	}

131	        ask.noteTipPageOpened()
132	        close()
133	    }
134	}
135	
136	// MARK: - The export doors
137	
138	/// The two places a person's export reaches Tips (TIP-4): the Export… sheet's
139	/// success and an Add to Queue job. `EditorViewController+Export.swift` is
140	/// the only caller; the agent's `export` never comes here. The ask, the
141	/// dialog and the queue are parameters so a probe runs both doors on its own.
142	/// Main thread.
143	final class TipsDoors {
144	    static let shared = TipsDoors()
145	
146	    private let ask: TipsAsk
147	    private let dialog: () -> TipsWindowController
148	    private let queue: ExportQueueController
149	    private var follower: TipsQueueFollower?
150	    private var queueObserver: NSObjectProtocol?
151	    /// The result sheets still up after a counted success, each waiting for
152	    /// its window's sheet to end.
153	    private var sheetEnds: [TipsSheetEnd] = []
154	
155	    init(
156	        ask: TipsAsk = .shared,
157	        dialog: @escaping () -> TipsWindowController = { TipsWindowController.shared },
158	        queue: ExportQueueController = .shared
159	    ) {
160	        self.ask = ask
161	        self.dialog = dialog
162	        self.queue = queue
163	    }
164	
165	    deinit {
166	        if let queueObserver { NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(queueObserver) }
167	    }
168	
169	    /// An Export… the person confirmed has succeeded: counted now. The ask
170	    /// waits until `window`'s sheet — the export's own result panel — ends,
171	    /// and one main-queue turn more so the sheet has left; with no sheet
172	    /// attached it is asked at once.
173	    func exportSucceeded(sheetOn window: NSWindow?) {
174	        ask.countExport()
175	        guard let window, window.attachedSheet != nil else {
176	            askIfDue()
177	            return
178	        }
179	        sheetEnds.append(
180	            TipsSheetEnd(window: window) { [weak self] watch in
181	                guard let self else { return }
182	                self.sheetEnds.removeAll { $0 === watch }
183	                self.askIfDue()
184	            })
185	    }
186	
187	    /// An Add to Queue job the person confirmed: followed to its end by id.
188	    /// A completion counts and asks; a cancel or a failure does neither.
189	    func follow(queueJob id: UInt64) {
190	        if follower == nil {
191	            follower = TipsQueueFollower(
192	                state: { [queue] in queue.job($0)?.state },
193	                completed: { [weak self] in
194	                    self?.ask.countExport()
195	                    self?.askIfDue()
196	                })
197	            queueObserver = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
198	                forName: ExportQueueController.didChangeNotification, object: queue, queue: nil
199	            ) { [weak self] _ in self?.follower?.settle() }
200	        }
201	        follower?.follow(id)
202	    }
203	
204	    /// Shows the dialog when the schedule says so, recording the ask at the
205	    /// moment it is shown.
206	    private func askIfDue() {
207	        guard ask.takeAsk() else { return }
208	        dialog().showAutomatic()
209	    }
210	}
211	
212	/// One wait for a window's sheet to end, then one main-queue turn.
213	private final class TipsSheetEnd: NSObject {
214	    private let then: (TipsSheetEnd) -> Void
215	
216	    init(window: NSWindow, then: @escaping (TipsSheetEnd) -> Void) {
217	        self.then = then
218	        super.init()
219	        NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
220	            self, selector: #selector(ended(_:)), name: NSWindow.didEndSheetNotification,
221	            object: window)
222	    }
223	
224	    @objc private func ended(_ note: Notification) {
225	        NotificationCenter.default.removeObserver(self)
226	        DispatchQueue.main.async { self.then(self) }
227	    }
228	}
229	
230	// MARK: - The command
231	
232	/// The command half, at the foot of the file that owns the feature
233	/// (`SettingsWindowController.swift`'s precedent): a nil-target selector, so
234	/// the editor's Tips button resolves it through the responder chain.
235	extension AppDelegate {
236	    @objc func showTips(_ sender: Any?) {
237	        TipsWindowController.shared.show()
238	    }
239	}

1	import AppKit
2	
3	extension AgentServer {
4	
5	    // MARK: - Export
6	
7	    /// `export` — ⌘E (`EditorViewController.exportProjectCommand` and
8	    /// `ExportSheetController`). The preset names the ENCODING — a container
9	    /// and a codec, nothing about size — and the size is the sheet's separate
10	    /// choice, in the Size popup's own vocabulary and defaulting as the popup
11	    /// does to its first row: the document's size, or an image format's cap.
12	    /// The CORE resolves both into concrete settings (`rc_export_settings`)
13	    /// that go to the same `Exporter.export` the sheet uses: there is exactly
14	    /// one writer, so an agent export and a menu export cannot disagree.
15	    ///
16	    /// Answers AT ONCE (spec §11 #326): every refusal is made here, before
17	    /// anything is queued — the arguments, the core's settings, the folder,
18	    /// the graphics gate, and the frame limit and same-shape rule
19	    /// (`Exporter.settingsRefusal`, #470) — and the export is then a job in the Export
20	    /// Queue, exactly as the sheet's Add to Queue makes one, answered as
21	    /// `{export_id, path, status}`. `export_status` follows the job and
22	    /// `cancel_export` stops it (`AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`); a failure
23	    /// while writing comes back from there. The queue window is not shown.
24	    ///
25	    /// One argument is NOT a setting and never reaches the core:
26	    /// `burn_in_timecode` is a recipe option (`RecipeOptions`), read below
27	    /// beside the overrides it deliberately does not join.
28	    ///
29	    /// The finished job's answer carries the sound the file actually holds —
30	    /// its integrated loudness and true peak, measured on the way through —
31	    /// for every format that has any, whether `loudness_lufs` was asked for
32	    /// or not, and, with `stems` (the sheet's Stems popup, spec §11 AU-108),
33	    /// each stem file beside the mix.
34	    func exportProject(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
35	        // The clock `export_status`'s `elapsed` runs on, read before any check.
36	        let started = ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
37	        let presetID = try requiredString(a, "preset")
38	        let path = try requiredString(a, "path")
39	        let wholeProject = (try stringArg(a, "range") ?? "project").lowercased()
40	        guard ["project", "in_out"].contains(wholeProject) else {
41	            throw ToolError(
42	                message: "range must be \"project\" (the whole timeline) or \"in_out\" "
43	                    + "(the in/out range set_range set), not \"\(wholeProject)\".")
44	        }
45	        // The export sheet's burn-in checkbox — and read HERE rather than
46	        // into `overrides` below, which is the whole of the decision. A
47	        // recipe option changes the PICTURE, so it travels with the
48	        // description of the picture: `export_overrides.rs` ignores a key it
49	        // does not know, on purpose, so a `burn_in_timecode` posted through
50	        // `rc_export_settings` would vanish without a word and this tool
51	        // would report success on an un-burnt file. It goes to `Exporter`
52	        // beside the settings instead (`RecipeOptions`, `Exporter.export`),
53	        // which is also what reaches GIF and APNG — those never go through
54	        // `ExportWriter` at all.
55	        let options = RecipeOptions(burnInTimecode: try boolArg(a, "burn_in_timecode") ?? false)
56	        let prepared = try onMain {
57	            () throws -> (ProjectDocument, ReelProject, [UInt32: URL], ExportSettings, GraphicSet?)
58	            in
59	            let document = try self.target(a)
60	            guard document.project.duration > 0 else {
61	                throw ToolError(message: "There is nothing on the timeline to export.")
62	            }
63	            let settings = try self.exportSettings(
64	                a, on: document, preset: presetID, range: wholeProject)
65	            return (
66	                document, document.project, document.mediaURLs(), settings,
67	                GraphicRegistry.shared.snapshot(for: document.recipeKey)
68	            )
69	        }
70	        let (document, project, urls, settings, graphics) = prepared
71	        let url = try Self.requireFolder(
72	            of: Self.destinationURL(path, extension: Exporter.fileExtension(for: settings)))
73	
74	        // The graphics gate, here rather than only in the writer: a module
75	        // that does not compile refuses the CALL, so nothing is queued that
76	        // could only fail (`Exporter.graphicsRefusal`, the writer's own gate).
77	        if let refusal = Exporter.graphicsRefusal(
78	            project: project, settings: settings, graphics: graphics)
79	        {

88	            // decoding the same media; the agent's does the same.
89	            self.editor(document)?.playback.pause()
90	            let id = ExportQueueController.shared.enqueue(
91	                project: project, urls: urls, settings: settings, to: url, options: options,
92	                graphics: graphics)

96	                Self.exportStatusWord($0.state)

101	    }

103	    /// The core's settings for `export`'s arguments, every override read as
104	    /// the sheet's popups spell it, and every refusal the tool's own. Main
105	    /// only. `range` is the call's `range`, already lower-cased.
106	    func exportSettings(
107	        _ a: [String: Any], on document: ProjectDocument, preset: String, range: String
108	    ) throws -> ExportSettings {
109	        // The Range popup of the export sheet, in the sheet's own terms:
110	        // "Whole project" is no override at all, "In/out range" is the
111	        // core's ONE nested `range` object (`export.rs`). The core snaps
112	        // it to the frame grid and clamps it to the project.
113	        var overrides: [String: Any] = [:]
114	        if range == "in_out" {
115	            guard let inOut = document.inOutRange, inOut.end > inOut.start else {
116	                throw ToolError(
117	                    message: "This project has no in/out range — set one with set_range "
118	                        + "{start, end}, or export with range \"project\".")
119	            }
120	            overrides["range"] = ["start": inOut.start, "duration": inOut.end - inOut.start]
121	        }
122	        // The sheet's Quality popup, in the core's own words: it resolves
123	        // a tier into these two keys and nothing else
124	        // (`ExportSheetController.overrides()`), so the agent spells them
125	        // the same way rather than re-deriving a rate from a tier name.
126	        // The core validates them — positive, u32 — and an unset key means
127	        // "the preset decides", which is what a nil bitrate already means
128	        // to the writer.
129	        if let video = try intArg(a, "video_bitrate") {
130	            overrides["video_bitrate"] = video
131	        }
132	        if let audio = try intArg(a, "audio_bitrate") {
133	            overrides["audio_bitrate"] = audio
134	        }
135	        // The sheet's Loudness popup, in the core's words again — and
136	        // through `doubleArg`, not `intArg`: −14.5 LUFS is a real request
137	        // and every one of these figures is a negative fraction. Neither
138	        // is validated here. `export_overrides.rs` owns the bounds
139	        // (−70…0 and −20…0) and names the offending value the way the
140	        // bitrate refusals do; either may come alone, the ceiling being
141	        // the master limiter's (spec §11 AU-27).
142	        // Restating a bound here would be a second spelling of it to
143	        // drift from the first.
144	        // The sheet sends both together and fixes the ceiling at
145	        // −1 dBTP; a caller that wants −0.3 or −2.0 says so here.
146	        if let target = try doubleArg(a, "loudness_lufs") {
147	            overrides["loudness_lufs"] = target
148	        }
149	        if let ceiling = try doubleArg(a, "peak_dbtp") {
150	            overrides["peak_dbtp"] = ceiling
151	        }
152	        // The sheet's Size popup: a row id, or "Custom…" as an explicit
153	        // [width, height]. Absent is no override at all, so the tool's
154	        // default and the sheet's are one code path in the core — the
155	        // document's size, or an image format's cap.
156	        if let size = try exportSizeArg(a, document.project, preset: preset) {
157	            overrides["width"] = size.width
158	            overrides["height"] = size.height
159	        }
160	        // The sheet's Dynamic Range popup (spec §11 HD-14 (c)), forwarded
161	        // unread: the core's reader and resolver own its three words, its
162	        // per-row defaults and both refusals, each in its own sentence.
163	        if let dynamicRange = a["dynamic_range"] {
164	            overrides["dynamic_range"] = dynamicRange
165	        }
166	        // The sheet's Speed popup (spec §11 CX-12 (2)), forwarded unread on the
167	        // same terms: the core reads the three words and refuses a row without one.
168	        if let speed = a["encoder_speed"] {
169	            overrides["encoder_speed"] = speed
170	        }
171	        // The sheet's Bit depth popup (spec §11 AU-29), forwarded unread on the
172	        // same terms: the core reads 16 or 24 and refuses a row without a depth.
173	        if let bits = a["audio_bits"] {
174	            overrides["audio_bits"] = bits
175	        }
176	        // The sheet's Stems popup (spec §11 AU-108), forwarded unread on the same
177	        // terms: the core reads "tracks" or "names", refuses a movie row, and refuses
178	        // a project with no track heard.
179	        if let stems = a["stems"] {
180	            overrides["stems"] = stems
181	        }
182	        do {
183	            return try ReelExport.settings(document.project, preset: preset, overrides: overrides)
184	        } catch {
185	            throw Self.coreRefusal(error)
186	        }
187	    }

189	    /// The file `export` writes for these arguments: the settings' own
190	    /// extension on `path`, so the assistant's question names what the tool
191	    /// will write (spec §11 AI-21 (c)). It throws what the tool would refuse.
192	    /// Main only, on the document the lane pinned.
193	    func exportDestination(_ a: [String: Any], on document: ProjectDocument) throws -> URL {
194	        let preset = try requiredString(a, "preset")
195	        let path = try requiredString(a, "path")
196	        let range = (try stringArg(a, "range") ?? "project").lowercased()
197	        let settings = try exportSettings(a, on: document, preset: preset, range: range)
198	        return Self.destinationURL(path, extension: Exporter.fileExtension(for: settings))

201	    /// The `size` argument of `export`, in the Size popup's vocabulary: a row
202	    /// id resolved through the same `rc_export_sizes` the popup is built from
203	    /// (`document`, `preset`, `2160p`, `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p` — `ExportSize`
204	    /// in `ReelCore.swift` says what each means, and `core/src/export_size.rs`
205	    /// why every document lists every row), or the popup's "Custom…" as an
206	    /// explicit `[width, height]`. nil when absent, which is no override: the
207	    /// core's default for the preset.
208	    ///
209	    /// A value that is neither is refused by NAME, never read as absent — the
210	    /// rule every reader in `AgentServer+Arguments.swift` keeps, and the root
211	    /// `CLAUDE.md`'s: a value a handler cannot read is refused by name, never
212	    /// dropped. A `size` dropped in silence would export at the wrong size
213	    /// and report success. A custom
214	    /// size outside the sheet's own field range is refused the same way,
215	    /// where the sheet clamps: a tool has no field to clamp in view of the
216	    /// caller, and the sheet's reason — a mistyped digit must not reach the
217	    /// encoder as a 300 000-pixel frame — holds for a model's typo too.
218	    private func exportSizeArg(
219	        _ a: [String: Any], _ project: ReelProject, preset: String
220	    ) throws -> (width: Int, height: Int)? {
221	        guard let raw = a["size"], !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }
222	        // The rows come first, whichever spelling follows: every refusal
223	        // below lists the ids from them rather than from a vocabulary
224	        // restated here, which could drift from the core's, and a preset the
225	        // core does not know is refused at this point in the same words
226	        // `exportProject` would use a call later.
227	        let rows: [ExportSize]
228	        do {
229	            rows = try ReelExport.sizes(project, preset: preset)
230	        } catch {
231	            throw Self.coreRefusal(error)
232	        }
233	        let ids = rows.map { $0.id }.joined(separator: ", ")
234	        if let id = raw as? String {
235	            guard let row = rows.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else {
236	                throw ToolError(
237	                    message: "No export size is called \"\(id)\" for \(preset). The sizes "
238	                        + "are: \(ids) — or pass [width, height].")
239	            }
240	            return (row.width, row.height)
241	        }
242	        if let array = raw as? [Any], array.count == 2 {
243	            let edges = array.compactMap(Self.wholeEdge)
244	            if edges.count == 2 {
245	                let range = ExportSheetController.sizeRange
246	                // Each refusal of a `size` offers the OTHER spelling: the
247	                // unknown-id one above names the custom form, and this one
248	                // names the rows, so a caller who meant a standard size and
249	                // reached for numbers has the ids in front of it.
250	                guard edges.allSatisfy(range.contains) else {
251	                    throw ToolError(
252	                        message: "A custom size must be \(range.lowerBound)…\(range.upperBound) "
253	                            + "px on each edge, not [\(edges[0]), \(edges[1])] — or pass a "
254	                            + "row: \(ids).")
255	                }
256	                return (edges[0], edges[1])
257	            }
258	        }
259	        throw ToolError(
260	            message: "size must be a row of the export sheet's Size popup — \(ids) — or "
261	                + "[width, height] in px, not \(Self.spelled(raw)).")
262	    }
263	
264	    /// One edge of a custom size as a whole number, or nil for a value that
265	    /// is not one — which sends the whole `size` to the refusal that names
266	    /// it. The coercion `intArg` applies holds: a string spelling of a whole
267	    /// number is a JSON-typing slip, not a different request. A fraction is
268	    /// refused rather than truncated, since 1920.5 is not a width the caller
269	    /// can have meant. So is a boolean: JSON's `true` arrives as an
270	    /// `NSNumber` like any other and would read as 1 through it, and the
271	    /// Core Foundation type is the one thing that still tells `true` from
272	    /// `1`.
273	    private static func wholeEdge(_ value: Any) -> Int? {
274	        if let number = value as? NSNumber {
275	            guard CFGetTypeID(number) != CFBooleanGetTypeID() else { return nil }
276	            let real = number.doubleValue
277	            return real.isFinite && real == real.rounded() ? number.intValue : nil
278	        }
279	        return (value as? String).flatMap(Int.init)
280	    }
281	
282	    /// A refusal from `rc_export_settings` or `rc_export_sizes` as the tool's
283	    /// error. The core's message passes through as it was, with one
284	    /// addition: an unknown preset id — the message that begins
285	    /// "unknown export preset", the same words from either call
286	    /// (`export.rs`) — gets the ids the table does take appended, because
287	    /// without them it is the one error a model cannot correct itself from,
288	    /// since nothing else lists the table. A refused bitrate or range keeps
289	    /// its own message alone: a list of presets under it would be a false
290	    /// lead.
291	    private static func coreRefusal(_ error: any Error) -> ToolError {
292	        let message = error.localizedDescription
293	        guard message.hasPrefix("unknown export preset") else {
294	            return ToolError(message: message)
295	        }
296	        let names = ReelExport.presets().map { $0.id }.joined(separator: ", ")
297	        return ToolError(message: "\(message). The presets are: \(names).")
298	    }
299	
300	    /// A caller's value as it was spelled, for a refusal that names it: its
301	    /// JSON where it is JSON, its Swift description otherwise.
302	    private static func spelled(_ raw: Any) -> String {
303	        guard JSONSerialization.isValidJSONObject([raw]),
304	            let data = try? JSONSerialization.data(
305	                withJSONObject: raw, options: [.fragmentsAllowed]),
306	            let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)
307	        else { return String(describing: raw) }
308	        return text
309	    }
310	}

5	/// The agent's half of the Export Queue (spec §11 #326): `export` enqueues a
6	/// job in `ExportQueueController.shared` and answers its id at once, and the
7	/// two tools here follow it. `export_status` mirrors Window ▸ Export Queue's
8	/// row for that job (`ExportQueueWindowController`) — its state, its progress
9	/// bar, its phase and its closing sentence — and `cancel_export` mirrors the
10	/// row's Cancel button, which calls the same `ExportQueueController.cancel`.
11	///
12	/// **Only ids `export` returned are reachable.** A person's own queued job has
13	/// no record here and is answered as unknown: the mirror follows what the
14	/// agent started, not the queue as a whole.
15	///
16	/// **A record outlives its row.** The queue drops a finished job on Remove or
17	/// Clear Finished, and an agent that asks after that must still hear how it
18	/// ended, so `AgentExports` copies each tracked job's state on every queue
19	/// change — synchronously, on main, inside the queue's own post — and stamps
20	/// the finish (its time and the file's size) on its first terminal sight.
21	/// Records last for the launch and hold no project handle or graphic set.
22	extension AgentServer {
23	
24	    /// `export_status {export_id}` — the row of Window ▸ Export Queue for a job
25	    /// `export` started, read now; it never waits.
26	    func exportStatus(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
27	        let id = try exportIDArg(a)
28	        guard let status = AgentExports.shared.status(id) else {
29	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
30	        }
31	        return try jsonResult(status)
32	    }
33	
34	    /// `cancel_export {export_id}` — the Export Queue row's Cancel. A queued
35	    /// or running job is cancelled through the queue (a running one answers
36	    /// through the writer, so it may still read `running` here); a finished
37	    /// one is left alone and answered as it is.
38	    func cancelExport(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
39	        let id = try exportIDArg(a)
40	        guard AgentExports.shared.status(id) != nil else {
41	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
42	        }
43	        if let job = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id), !job.state.isFinished {
44	            ExportQueueController.shared.cancel(id)
45	        }
46	        guard let status = AgentExports.shared.status(id) else {
47	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
48	        }
49	        return try jsonResult(status)
50	    }
51	
52	    /// The word a status answer spells a queue state with.
53	    static func exportStatusWord(_ state: ExportQueueController.State) -> String {
54	        switch state {
55	        case .waiting: return "queued"
56	        case .running: return "running"
57	        case .completed: return "done"
58	        case .failed: return "failed"
59	        case .cancelled: return "cancelled"
60	        }
61	    }
62	
63	    /// `export_id`, required and whole. An id below 1 is no id `export`
64	    /// returned, so it is refused as an unknown one rather than converted.
65	    private func exportIDArg(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> UInt64 {
66	        guard let raw = try intArg(a, "export_id") else {
67	            throw ToolError(message: "Missing required argument: export_id")
68	        }
69	        guard raw >= 1 else {
70	            throw ToolError(
71	                message: "No export this launch has export_id \(raw) — ids come from export "
72	                    + "and last until Frame Job quits.")
73	        }
74	        return UInt64(raw)
75	    }
76	
77	    private static func unknownExport(_ id: UInt64) -> ToolError {
78	        ToolError(
79	            message: "No export this launch has export_id \(id) — ids come from export and "
80	                + "last until Frame Job quits.")
81	    }
82	}

84	/// What `AgentExports` keeps of one tracked job: the queue row's fields as
85	/// last seen, plus what the `done` answer needs that the job does not carry.
86	private struct AgentExportRecord {
87	    let settings: ExportSettings
88	    let burnInTimecode: Bool
89	    /// `systemUptime` at the `export` handler's first line.
90	    let started: TimeInterval
91	    var state: ExportQueueController.State
92	    var progress: Double
93	    var phase: String?
94	    var message: String?
95	    var destination: URL
96	    var loudness: ExportLoudness?
97	    var graphicWarnings: [ExportGraphicWarning]
98	    /// The media whose cursor file was not drawn (spec §11 CU-37 (c)).
99	    var cursorWarnings: [ExportCursorWarning]
100	    /// `systemUptime` at the first terminal sight, nil until then.
101	    var finished: TimeInterval?
102	    /// The file's size as read at that finish.
103	    var bytes: Int = 0
104	
105	    mutating func copy(_ job: ExportQueueController.Job) {
106	        state = job.state
107	        progress = job.progress
108	        phase = job.phase
109	        message = job.message
110	        destination = job.destination
111	        loudness = job.loudness
112	        graphicWarnings = job.graphicWarnings
113	        cursorWarnings = job.cursorWarnings
114	        guard job.state.isFinished, finished == nil else { return }
115	        finished = ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
116	        bytes =
117	            (try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: job.destination.path)[.size])
118	            .flatMap { ($0 as? NSNumber)?.intValue } ?? 0
119	    }
120	}
121	
122	/// The records of every export the agent started this launch, by the queue's
123	/// job id. Main thread only, like the queue it reads.
124	final class AgentExports {
125	    static let shared = AgentExports()
126	
127	    private var records: [UInt64: AgentExportRecord] = [:]
128	    private var observer: NSObjectProtocol?
129	
130	    private init() {
131	        // `queue: nil` runs the block synchronously inside the queue's own
132	        // post, so a terminal state is copied before any Remove can drop it.
133	        observer = NotificationCenter.default.addObserver(
134	            forName: ExportQueueController.didChangeNotification,
135	            object: ExportQueueController.shared, queue: nil
136	        ) { [weak self] _ in self?.refresh() }
137	    }
138	
139	    /// Starts following a job `export` just enqueued. Reads it AT ONCE: an
140	    /// early refusal finishes inside `enqueue`, before this is called, so its
141	    /// terminal post has already gone by.
142	    func track(
143	        _ id: UInt64, settings: ExportSettings, burnInTimecode: Bool, started: TimeInterval
144	    ) {
145	        // Never nil: `enqueue` appends the job before it returns, an early
146	        // refusal only finishes it in place, and the only removals (`remove`,
147	        // `clearFinished`) are the queue window's button actions, which cannot
148	        // run inside the one main-thread block that enqueues and calls this.
149	        guard let job = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id) else { return }
150	        var record = AgentExportRecord(
151	            settings: settings, burnInTimecode: burnInTimecode, started: started,
152	            state: job.state, progress: job.progress, phase: job.phase, message: job.message,
153	            destination: job.destination, loudness: job.loudness,
154	            graphicWarnings: job.graphicWarnings, cursorWarnings: job.cursorWarnings)
155	        record.copy(job)
156	        records[id] = record
157	    }
158	
159	    /// The `export_status` answer for `id`, or nil for an id `export` never
160	    /// returned this launch.
161	    func status(_ id: UInt64) -> [String: Any]? {
162	        guard let record = records[id] else { return nil }
163	        let end = record.finished ?? ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
164	        var answer: [String: Any] = [:]
165	        switch record.state {
166	        case .running:
167	            answer["progress"] = record.progress
168	            if let phase = record.phase { answer["phase"] = phase }
169	        case .completed:
170	            answer = AgentServer.exportResult(
171	                settings: record.settings, burnInTimecode: record.burnInTimecode,
172	                path: record.destination.path, bytes: record.bytes, loudness: record.loudness,
173	                graphicWarnings: record.graphicWarnings, cursorWarnings: record.cursorWarnings)
174	            // The queue row's own success sentence (spec §11 #395), as the
175	            // row held it at the finish; `exportResult`'s keys stay the ones
176	            // `export` answered before #326.
177	            if let message = record.message { answer["message"] = message }
178	        case .failed, .cancelled:
179	            answer["reason"] = record.message ?? ""
180	        case .waiting:
181	            // The memory hold's sentence, present only while held (spec §11 CX-18).
182	            if let held = record.message { answer["waiting"] = held }
183	        }
184	        if record.state == .waiting || record.state == .running,
185	            let seconds = ExportEncoderCosts.estimatedSeconds(for: record.settings)
186	        {
187	            answer["estimated_seconds"] = Int(seconds.rounded())
188	        }
189	        answer["export_id"] = id
190	        answer["status"] = AgentServer.exportStatusWord(record.state)
191	        answer["path"] = record.destination.path
192	        answer["elapsed"] = ((end - record.started) * 1000).rounded() / 1000
193	        return answer
194	    }
195	
196	    /// Copies every unfinished tracked job from the queue.
197	    private func refresh() {
198	        let queue = ExportQueueController.shared
199	        for (id, record) in records where record.finished == nil {
200	            guard let job = queue.job(id) else { continue }
201	            var updated = record
202	            updated.copy(job)
203	            records[id] = updated
204	        }
205	    }
206	}

7	    /// `export` — ⌘E (`EditorViewController.exportProjectCommand` and
8	    /// `ExportSheetController`). The preset names the ENCODING — a container
9	    /// and a codec, nothing about size — and the size is the sheet's separate
10	    /// choice, in the Size popup's own vocabulary and defaulting as the popup
11	    /// does to its first row: the document's size, or an image format's cap.
12	    /// The CORE resolves both into concrete settings (`rc_export_settings`)
13	    /// that go to the same `Exporter.export` the sheet uses: there is exactly
14	    /// one writer, so an agent export and a menu export cannot disagree.
15	    ///
16	    /// Answers AT ONCE (spec §11 #326): every refusal is made here, before
17	    /// anything is queued — the arguments, the core's settings, the folder,
18	    /// the graphics gate, and the frame limit and same-shape rule
19	    /// (`Exporter.settingsRefusal`, #470) — and the export is then a job in the Export
20	    /// Queue, exactly as the sheet's Add to Queue makes one, answered as
21	    /// `{export_id, path, status}`. `export_status` follows the job and
22	    /// `cancel_export` stops it (`AgentServer+ExportStatus.swift`); a failure
23	    /// while writing comes back from there. The queue window is not shown.
24	    ///
25	    /// One argument is NOT a setting and never reaches the core:
26	    /// `burn_in_timecode` is a recipe option (`RecipeOptions`), read below
27	    /// beside the overrides it deliberately does not join.
28	    ///
29	    /// The finished job's answer carries the sound the file actually holds —
30	    /// its integrated loudness and true peak, measured on the way through —
31	    /// for every format that has any, whether `loudness_lufs` was asked for
32	    /// or not, and, with `stems` (the sheet's Stems popup, spec §11 AU-108),
33	    /// each stem file beside the mix.
34	    func exportProject(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
35	        // The clock `export_status`'s `elapsed` runs on, read before any check.
36	        let started = ProcessInfo.processInfo.systemUptime
37	        let presetID = try requiredString(a, "preset")
38	        let path = try requiredString(a, "path")
39	        let wholeProject = (try stringArg(a, "range") ?? "project").lowercased()
40	        guard ["project", "in_out"].contains(wholeProject) else {
41	            throw ToolError(
42	                message: "range must be \"project\" (the whole timeline) or \"in_out\" "
43	                    + "(the in/out range set_range set), not \"\(wholeProject)\".")
44	        }
45	        // The export sheet's burn-in checkbox — and read HERE rather than
46	        // into `overrides` below, which is the whole of the decision. A
47	        // recipe option changes the PICTURE, so it travels with the
48	        // description of the picture: `export_overrides.rs` ignores a key it
49	        // does not know, on purpose, so a `burn_in_timecode` posted through
50	        // `rc_export_settings` would vanish without a word and this tool
51	        // would report success on an un-burnt file. It goes to `Exporter`
52	        // beside the settings instead (`RecipeOptions`, `Exporter.export`),
53	        // which is also what reaches GIF and APNG — those never go through
54	        // `ExportWriter` at all.
55	        let options = RecipeOptions(burnInTimecode: try boolArg(a, "burn_in_timecode") ?? false)
56	        let prepared = try onMain {
57	            () throws -> (ProjectDocument, ReelProject, [UInt32: URL], ExportSettings, GraphicSet?)
58	            in
59	            let document = try self.target(a)

103	    /// The core's settings for `export`'s arguments, every override read as
104	    /// the sheet's popups spell it, and every refusal the tool's own. Main
105	    /// only. `range` is the call's `range`, already lower-cased.
106	    func exportSettings(
107	        _ a: [String: Any], on document: ProjectDocument, preset: String, range: String
108	    ) throws -> ExportSettings {
109	        // The Range popup of the export sheet, in the sheet's own terms:
110	        // "Whole project" is no override at all, "In/out range" is the
111	        // core's ONE nested `range` object (`export.rs`). The core snaps
112	        // it to the frame grid and clamps it to the project.
113	        var overrides: [String: Any] = [:]
114	        if range == "in_out" {
115	            guard let inOut = document.inOutRange, inOut.end > inOut.start else {
116	                throw ToolError(
117	                    message: "This project has no in/out range — set one with set_range "
118	                        + "{start, end}, or export with range \"project\".")
119	            }
120	            overrides["range"] = ["start": inOut.start, "duration": inOut.end - inOut.start]
121	        }
122	        // The sheet's Quality popup, in the core's own words: it resolves
123	        // a tier into these two keys and nothing else
124	        // (`ExportSheetController.overrides()`), so the agent spells them
125	        // the same way rather than re-deriving a rate from a tier name.
126	        // The core validates them — positive, u32 — and an unset key means
127	        // "the preset decides", which is what a nil bitrate already means
128	        // to the writer.
129	        if let video = try intArg(a, "video_bitrate") {
130	            overrides["video_bitrate"] = video
131	        }
132	        if let audio = try intArg(a, "audio_bitrate") {
133	            overrides["audio_bitrate"] = audio
134	        }
135	        // The sheet's Loudness popup, in the core's words again — and
136	        // through `doubleArg`, not `intArg`: −14.5 LUFS is a real request
137	        // and every one of these figures is a negative fraction. Neither
138	        // is validated here. `export_overrides.rs` owns the bounds
139	        // (−70…0 and −20…0) and names the offending value the way the
140	        // bitrate refusals do; either may come alone, the ceiling being
141	        // the master limiter's (spec §11 AU-27).
142	        // Restating a bound here would be a second spelling of it to
143	        // drift from the first.
144	        // The sheet sends both together and fixes the ceiling at
145	        // −1 dBTP; a caller that wants −0.3 or −2.0 says so here.
146	        if let target = try doubleArg(a, "loudness_lufs") {
147	            overrides["loudness_lufs"] = target
148	        }
149	        if let ceiling = try doubleArg(a, "peak_dbtp") {
150	            overrides["peak_dbtp"] = ceiling
151	        }
152	        // The sheet's Size popup: a row id, or "Custom…" as an explicit
153	        // [width, height]. Absent is no override at all, so the tool's
154	        // default and the sheet's are one code path in the core — the
155	        // document's size, or an image format's cap.
156	        if let size = try exportSizeArg(a, document.project, preset: preset) {
157	            overrides["width"] = size.width
158	            overrides["height"] = size.height
159	        }
160	        // The sheet's Dynamic Range popup (spec §11 HD-14 (c)), forwarded
161	        // unread: the core's reader and resolver own its three words, its
162	        // per-row defaults and both refusals, each in its own sentence.
163	        if let dynamicRange = a["dynamic_range"] {
164	            overrides["dynamic_range"] = dynamicRange
165	        }
166	        // The sheet's Speed popup (spec §11 CX-12 (2)), forwarded unread on the
167	        // same terms: the core reads the three words and refuses a row without one.
168	        if let speed = a["encoder_speed"] {
169	            overrides["encoder_speed"] = speed
170	        }
171	        // The sheet's Bit depth popup (spec §11 AU-29), forwarded unread on the
172	        // same terms: the core reads 16 or 24 and refuses a row without a depth.
173	        if let bits = a["audio_bits"] {
174	            overrides["audio_bits"] = bits
175	        }
176	        // The sheet's Stems popup (spec §11 AU-108), forwarded unread on the same
177	        // terms: the core reads "tracks" or "names", refuses a movie row, and refuses
178	        // a project with no track heard.
179	        if let stems = a["stems"] {
180	            overrides["stems"] = stems
181	        }
182	        do {
183	            return try ReelExport.settings(document.project, preset: preset, overrides: overrides)
184	        } catch {
185	            throw Self.coreRefusal(error)
186	        }
187	    }

189	    /// The file `export` writes for these arguments: the settings' own
190	    /// extension on `path`, so the assistant's question names what the tool
191	    /// will write (spec §11 AI-21 (c)). It throws what the tool would refuse.
192	    /// Main only, on the document the lane pinned.
193	    func exportDestination(_ a: [String: Any], on document: ProjectDocument) throws -> URL {
194	        let preset = try requiredString(a, "preset")
195	        let path = try requiredString(a, "path")
196	        let range = (try stringArg(a, "range") ?? "project").lowercased()
197	        let settings = try exportSettings(a, on: document, preset: preset, range: range)
198	        return Self.destinationURL(path, extension: Exporter.fileExtension(for: settings))
199	    }

201	    /// The `size` argument of `export`, in the Size popup's vocabulary: a row
202	    /// id resolved through the same `rc_export_sizes` the popup is built from
203	    /// (`document`, `preset`, `2160p`, `1440p`, `1080p`, `720p` — `ExportSize`
204	    /// in `ReelCore.swift` says what each means, and `core/src/export_size.rs`
205	    /// why every document lists every row), or the popup's "Custom…" as an
206	    /// explicit `[width, height]`. nil when absent, which is no override: the
207	    /// core's default for the preset.
208	    ///
209	    /// A value that is neither is refused by NAME, never read as absent — the
210	    /// rule every reader in `AgentServer+Arguments.swift` keeps, and the root
211	    /// `CLAUDE.md`'s: a value a handler cannot read is refused by name, never
212	    /// dropped. A `size` dropped in silence would export at the wrong size
213	    /// and report success. A custom
214	    /// size outside the sheet's own field range is refused the same way,
215	    /// where the sheet clamps: a tool has no field to clamp in view of the
216	    /// caller, and the sheet's reason — a mistyped digit must not reach the
217	    /// encoder as a 300 000-pixel frame — holds for a model's typo too.
218	    private func exportSizeArg(
219	        _ a: [String: Any], _ project: ReelProject, preset: String
220	    ) throws -> (width: Int, height: Int)? {
221	        guard let raw = a["size"], !(raw is NSNull) else { return nil }
222	        // The rows come first, whichever spelling follows: every refusal
223	        // below lists the ids from them rather than from a vocabulary
224	        // restated here, which could drift from the core's, and a preset the
225	        // core does not know is refused at this point in the same words
226	        // `exportProject` would use a call later.
227	        let rows: [ExportSize]
228	        do {
229	            rows = try ReelExport.sizes(project, preset: preset)
230	        } catch {
231	            throw Self.coreRefusal(error)
232	        }
233	        let ids = rows.map { $0.id }.joined(separator: ", ")
234	        if let id = raw as? String {
235	            guard let row = rows.first(where: { $0.id == id }) else {
236	                throw ToolError(
237	                    message: "No export size is called \"\(id)\" for \(preset). The sizes "
238	                        + "are: \(ids) — or pass [width, height].")
239	            }
240	            return (row.width, row.height)
241	        }
242	        if let array = raw as? [Any], array.count == 2 {
243	            let edges = array.compactMap(Self.wholeEdge)
244	            if edges.count == 2 {
245	                let range = ExportSheetController.sizeRange
246	                // Each refusal of a `size` offers the OTHER spelling: the
247	                // unknown-id one above names the custom form, and this one
248	                // names the rows, so a caller who meant a standard size and
249	                // reached for numbers has the ids in front of it.
250	                guard edges.allSatisfy(range.contains) else {
251	                    throw ToolError(
252	                        message: "A custom size must be \(range.lowerBound)…\(range.upperBound) "
253	                            + "px on each edge, not [\(edges[0]), \(edges[1])] — or pass a "
254	                            + "row: \(ids).")
255	                }
256	                return (edges[0], edges[1])
257	            }
258	        }
259	        throw ToolError(
260	            message: "size must be a row of the export sheet's Size popup — \(ids) — or "
261	                + "[width, height] in px, not \(Self.spelled(raw)).")
262	    }
263	
264	    /// One edge of a custom size as a whole number, or nil for a value that
265	    /// is not one — which sends the whole `size` to the refusal that names
266	    /// it. The coercion `intArg` applies holds: a string spelling of a whole
267	    /// number is a JSON-typing slip, not a different request. A fraction is
268	    /// refused rather than truncated, since 1920.5 is not a width the caller
269	    /// can have meant. So is a boolean: JSON's `true` arrives as an
270	    /// `NSNumber` like any other and would read as 1 through it, and the
271	    /// Core Foundation type is the one thing that still tells `true` from
272	    /// `1`.
273	    private static func wholeEdge(_ value: Any) -> Int? {
274	        if let number = value as? NSNumber {
275	            guard CFGetTypeID(number) != CFBooleanGetTypeID() else { return nil }
276	            let real = number.doubleValue
277	            return real.isFinite && real == real.rounded() ? number.intValue : nil
278	        }
279	        return (value as? String).flatMap(Int.init)
280	    }
281	
282	    /// A refusal from `rc_export_settings` or `rc_export_sizes` as the tool's
283	    /// error. The core's message passes through as it was, with one
284	    /// addition: an unknown preset id — the message that begins
285	    /// "unknown export preset", the same words from either call
286	    /// (`export.rs`) — gets the ids the table does take appended, because
287	    /// without them it is the one error a model cannot correct itself from,
288	    /// since nothing else lists the table. A refused bitrate or range keeps
289	    /// its own message alone: a list of presets under it would be a false
290	    /// lead.
291	    private static func coreRefusal(_ error: any Error) -> ToolError {
292	        let message = error.localizedDescription
293	        guard message.hasPrefix("unknown export preset") else {
294	            return ToolError(message: message)
295	        }
296	        let names = ReelExport.presets().map { $0.id }.joined(separator: ", ")
297	        return ToolError(message: "\(message). The presets are: \(names).")
298	    }
299	
300	    /// A caller's value as it was spelled, for a refusal that names it: its
301	    /// JSON where it is JSON, its Swift description otherwise.
302	    private static func spelled(_ raw: Any) -> String {
303	        guard JSONSerialization.isValidJSONObject([raw]),
304	            let data = try? JSONSerialization.data(
305	                withJSONObject: raw, options: [.fragmentsAllowed]),
306	            let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)
307	        else { return String(describing: raw) }
308	        return text
309	    }
310	}

3	// MARK: - export_status and cancel_export
4	
5	/// The agent's half of the Export Queue (spec §11 #326): `export` enqueues a
6	/// job in `ExportQueueController.shared` and answers its id at once, and the
7	/// two tools here follow it. `export_status` mirrors Window ▸ Export Queue's
8	/// row for that job (`ExportQueueWindowController`) — its state, its progress
9	/// bar, its phase and its closing sentence — and `cancel_export` mirrors the
10	/// row's Cancel button, which calls the same `ExportQueueController.cancel`.
11	///
12	/// **Only ids `export` returned are reachable.** A person's own queued job has
13	/// no record here and is answered as unknown: the mirror follows what the
14	/// agent started, not the queue as a whole.
15	///
16	/// **A record outlives its row.** The queue drops a finished job on Remove or
17	/// Clear Finished, and an agent that asks after that must still hear how it
18	/// ended, so `AgentExports` copies each tracked job's state on every queue
19	/// change — synchronously, on main, inside the queue's own post — and stamps
20	/// the finish (its time and the file's size) on its first terminal sight.
21	/// Records last for the launch and hold no project handle or graphic set.
22	extension AgentServer {
23	
24	    /// `export_status {export_id}` — the row of Window ▸ Export Queue for a job
25	    /// `export` started, read now; it never waits.
26	    func exportStatus(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
27	        let id = try exportIDArg(a)
28	        guard let status = AgentExports.shared.status(id) else {
29	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
30	        }
31	        return try jsonResult(status)
32	    }
33	
34	    /// `cancel_export {export_id}` — the Export Queue row's Cancel. A queued
35	    /// or running job is cancelled through the queue (a running one answers
36	    /// through the writer, so it may still read `running` here); a finished
37	    /// one is left alone and answered as it is.
38	    func cancelExport(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> String {
39	        let id = try exportIDArg(a)
40	        guard AgentExports.shared.status(id) != nil else {
41	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
42	        }
43	        if let job = ExportQueueController.shared.job(id), !job.state.isFinished {
44	            ExportQueueController.shared.cancel(id)
45	        }
46	        guard let status = AgentExports.shared.status(id) else {
47	            throw Self.unknownExport(id)
48	        }
49	        return try jsonResult(status)
50	    }
51	
52	    /// The word a status answer spells a queue state with.
53	    static func exportStatusWord(_ state: ExportQueueController.State) -> String {
54	        switch state {
55	        case .waiting: return "queued"
56	        case .running: return "running"
57	        case .completed: return "done"
58	        case .failed: return "failed"
59	        case .cancelled: return "cancelled"
60	        }
61	    }
62	
63	    /// `export_id`, required and whole. An id below 1 is no id `export`
64	    /// returned, so it is refused as an unknown one rather than converted.
65	    private func exportIDArg(_ a: [String: Any]) throws -> UInt64 {
66	        guard let raw = try intArg(a, "export_id") else {
67	            throw ToolError(message: "Missing required argument: export_id")
68	        }
69	        guard raw >= 1 else {
70	            throw ToolError(
71	                message: "No export this launch has export_id \(raw) — ids come from export "
72	                    + "and last until Frame Job quits.")
73	        }
74	        return UInt64(raw)
75	    }
76	
77	    private static func unknownExport(_ id: UInt64) -> ToolError {
78	        ToolError(
79	            message: "No export this launch has export_id \(id) — ids come from export and "
80	                + "last until Frame Job quits.")
81	    }
82	}
